basis: Cash net profit after tax (cash NPAT) from continuing operations, full year ended 30 June 2026 (FY26) versus full year ended 30 June 2025 (FY25). Financial results are presented on a continuing-operations basis and FY25 comparatives are restated to conform to FY26 presentation; the restatement does not change the FY25 group cash NPAT total of $10,252m. Cash NPAT including discontinued operations moved from $10,253m to $10,982m (+$729m, +7%); the $1m difference sits in a discontinued-operations cash NPAT line that is nil in FY26.

statutory_movement.note: Statutory NPAT from continuing operations rose $778m or 8%, from $10,133m to $10,911m. Statutory NPAT including discontinued operations rose $750m or 7%, from $10,116m to $10,866m, after a $45m non-cash loss on the disposal of Colonial First State (CFS) in the discontinued-operations line. The ASX Announcement headlines the continuing-operations statutory figure ($10,911m, +8%) alongside cash NPAT ($10,982m, +7%).

cash_to_statutory_reconciliation.narrative: Statutory NPAT (continuing operations) grew $48m faster than cash NPAT (continuing operations) because the after-tax drag from non-cash items narrowed from -$119m in FY25 to -$71m in FY26. FY25's drag was dominated by a $172m after-tax loss on acquisition, disposal, closure and demerger of businesses (Bank of Hangzhou and other divestments), partly offset by +$53m of favourable hedging and IFRS volatility. FY26's smaller -$71m drag comprised a -$17m disposal loss and a -$54m negative swing in hedging and IFRS volatility. On a total basis (including discontinued operations), the CFS disposal added a further -$45m non-cash item in FY26 (vs -$18m in FY25), which is why the total-basis statutory movement (+$750m, +7%) is $28m lower than the continuing-operations statutory movement (+$778m, +8%).

drivers.name: Net interest income
drivers.narrative: Net interest income rose 7% to $25,586m, the single largest driver of the cash NPAT increase. The gain came almost entirely from volume: average interest earning assets rose $92bn (8%) to $1,246bn, with average lending assets up $60bn (7%) - home loans +$32bn (5%), business and corporate loans +$27bn (10%). Net interest margin fell 3bpts to 2.05%, but the bank states margin was stable excluding liquid-asset growth. The bank's own NIM bridge: asset pricing -5bpts (home lending -4bpts, business/institutional -1bpt, both from competition), funding costs flat, portfolio mix +2bpts, basis risk flat, capital/replicating/other +5bpts (replicating portfolio +4bpts, capital hedges +1bpt), Treasury and Markets -2bpts, liquids -2bpts (net -3bpts).
citations: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p28: 'Net interest income was $25,586 million, an increase of $1,563 million or 7% on the prior year. The result was driven by a $92 billion or 8% increase in average interest earning assets to $1,246 billion, partly offset by a 3 basis point decrease in net interest margin to 2.05%.'

drivers.name: Other operating income
drivers.narrative: Other operating income rose 4% to $4,638m. Commissions rose $135m (6%) to $2,234m on higher insurance income - including a milestone payment from the sale of Commonwealth Insurance Limited (CommInsure General Insurance) - higher equities income, and higher syndication fees, partly offset by lower deposit fees, credit card fees and FX income. Other income rose $46m (42%) to $156m, mainly a fair value gain on the Gemini investment following its IPO, partly offset by lower Structured Asset Finance revenue after the aircraft lease portfolio sale. Lending fees +$12m, funds management +$12m, trading income -$9m. The one-off gains (CommInsure milestone, Gemini fair value gain) sit inside this driver and are not separately quantified by the bank.

drivers.name: Underlying operating expenses
drivers.narrative: Underlying operating expenses (excluding restructuring and notable items) rose 6% to $13,585m, the largest drag on the movement. The bank's own bridge: inflation +$455m, investment in technology +$444m, investment in frontline and operations +$128m, other +$96m, productivity -$404m. By category: IT services +$393m (16%, cloud computing volumes, software licensing, amortisation, infrastructure/resilience/AI investment); staff expenses +$288m (4%, wage inflation and average FTE up 1,760 to 51,756); other expenses +$57m (4%, marketing); occupancy -$19m (2%, lower depreciation and favourable FX). Favourable FX partly offset staff and occupancy costs but is not quantified separately by the bank.

drivers.name: Loan impairment expense
drivers.narrative: Loan impairment expense rose 9% to $788m (loan loss rate 8bpts of average GLAA, up 1bpt), reflecting higher collective provisions from portfolio growth, geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty. By division: Retail Banking Services +$106m (to $378m, cost-of-living pressures), New Zealand +$11m (to $66m), Corporate Centre +$6m, partly offset by Business Banking -$45m (to $310m, lower individually assessed charges and higher write-backs) and Institutional Banking and Markets -$16m (to $33m, release of individually assessed provisions). The divisional moves sum to the $62m group increase.

drivers.name: Corporate tax expense
drivers.narrative: Corporate tax expense rose 5% to $4,699m on higher pre-tax profit. The effective tax rate (cash basis) fell 50bpts, from 30.5% to 30.0%, mainly due to lower non-deductible expenses. Because tax expense (5%) grew slower than pre-tax profit (6%, net profit before tax $14,743m to $15,681m), the lower effective rate softened - but did not eliminate - the tax drag on cash NPAT growth.
citations: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p35: 'Corporate tax expense was $4,699 million, an increase of $208 million or 5% on the prior year, reflecting a 30.0% effective tax rate.'

notable_items.narrative: Restructuring and notable items, disclosed separately within operating expenses, rose from $130m in FY25 to $170m in FY26 - a $40m incremental pre-tax drag on cash NPAT versus the prior year. FY26 items (bank does not split the $170m by component): provisions for the settlement of NZ legal proceedings - most likely the ASB Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act 2003 (CCCFA) class action, settled for NZ$135.6m and approved by the High Court of New Zealand on 14 January 2026; an additional goodwill payment to certain customers following ASIC's Better Banking review; and domestic customer remediation. FY25 items were split by the bank: domestic customer remediation $52m, NZ remediation $33m, and a Bankwest restructuring provision $45m (summing to $130m).

FY25 related to domestic and NZ customer remediation as well as a Bankwest restructuring provision.'

A settlement was reached ... ASB agreeing to pay NZ$135.6 million ... The settlement was approved by the High Court of New Zealand on 14 January 2026.'

notable_items.limitation: The FY26 $170m is not broken down by the bank into its three named components (NZ legal settlement, ASIC goodwill payment, domestic remediation), so the $40m incremental drag cannot be attributed to a single named item with certainty; the NZ CCCFA class-action link is inferred from the litigation note on PDF p138, not stated verbatim as the source of the $170m.

residual_note: Quantified drivers sum exactly to the movement: +1,563 (NII) + 196 (other operating income) - 719 (underlying operating expenses) - 40 (restructuring and notable items) - 62 (loan impairment expense) - 208 (corporate tax expense) = +730. No unexplained residual.

disagreements.topic: Loan impairment expense growth rate: 9% vs 8.5%
values: 9% - CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p16 and p34: 'Loan impairment expense was $788 million, an increase of $62 million or 9% on the prior year.'
disagreements.preferred: Use the dollar values ($726m to $788m, +$62m). Both percentages derive from the same underlying figures (+62/726 = 8.54%); the profit announcement rounds to the nearest whole percentage point (9%) while the results presentation shows one decimal place (8.5%).
disagreements.explanation: No underlying figures conflict; only the displayed precision of the percentage differs between documents.

disagreements.topic: Headline statutory NPAT: continuing-operations figure vs total figure
values: $10,911m, up 8% - CBA-FY26-asx-announcement.pdf, PDF p1: 'Statutory NPAT ... $10,911m ... 8% on FY25' (continuing operations)
$10,866m, up 7% - CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p16: 'Net profit after tax – statutory basis 10,866 7' (including discontinued operations)
disagreements.preferred: For comparison against cash NPAT, use the continuing-operations pair ($10,133m to $10,911m), because cash NPAT is also headlined by the bank on a continuing-operations basis ($10,252m to $10,982m). The ASX Announcement's front-page figure is on the same basis as the cash NPAT figure it is quoted alongside.
disagreements.explanation: Both figures are correct and fully disclosed; they differ only in whether the $45m discontinued-operations (CFS disposal) loss is included.

limitations: The bank does not split the $170m FY26 restructuring and notable items charge by its three named components (NZ legal settlement, ASIC-related goodwill payment, domestic remediation); the $40m year-on-year increase in this line cannot be attributed to a single component with certainty.
The one-off gains embedded in other operating income (CommInsure General Insurance milestone payment; Gemini IPO fair value gain) are named but not individually quantified by the bank.
The favourable FX offset embedded in operating expenses (staff and occupancy lines) is described qualitatively but not quantified by the bank.
Net interest margin drivers are disclosed only in basis points, not dollars; the bank does not publish a dollar-value split of the $1,563m NII increase between volume and margin/rate effects.

All quantified drivers are on the bank's cash, continuing-operations basis with FY25 restated comparatives; the sign convention for expense and impairment drivers is the pre-tax P&L line impact, with the associated tax effect captured separately inside the corporate tax expense driver.

Figures were extracted from the PDF text layer of the four named source documents only; chart-only values (e.g. NIM bridge, expense bridge) were cross-checked against, and matched, the same figures printed in text or tables in at least one of the four documents.
